Amazing game don't be put off by others. 

Very similar to the others but that's not a bad thing.

If you're like me and want more than 60fps you will have to change it manually which is a bit of a nightmare but it's easy to do. Just do the following;

1 - Go to the below directory

C:\Users\[USERNAME]\AppData\Local\Robot Entertainment\Orcs Must Die! 3\Saved\Config\WindowsNoEditor\GameUserSettings.ini

If AppData doesn't show up, go to "View" at the top and check the "Hidden Items" box. Alternatively, open WIN+R and type "%AppData%". Go back one folder and go into "Local".

2 - Open this file in Notepad

3 - CTRL+F -> Search "Frame" -> "Find Next" until you reach "FrameRameLimit"

4 - Set this value to your desired Frame Rate (e.g. 120, 144, 240, 360)

5 - Save the file and close -> Right click "Properties" -> Set to "Read Only"

<3

This is a tough one.  I avoided the Unchained disaster entirely, waited for Steam release for OMD3.  It feels more like a subexpansion of OMD2 more than anything.  The new things they try end up hindering the game in my opinion.  As one other reviewer mentioned, its less an action tower defense game with some 3PV action, more of a full 3PV action game, with a few towers to support.

I played the previous ones and many others as a strategist, I like to set up funnels, kill boxes, and trap layers that handle the mobs for me - minimal help from me needed.  OMD3 does not permit this.  As a matter of fact, many early waves on many maps you simply have too little resources to even set up a basic trap box and you have to take out the entire wave by yourself.  Not a terrible thing, but not a thing many Orcs! players likely would have wanted in a sequel.

They don't give enough resources, and the traps for the large part are underpowered.  The devs seem to really want you to engage in high intensity close combat personally and I don't like that.  The winning combo for me was tar, blockades and archers.  Everything else is superfluous.  You get an area where you can slow them down and the archers will machinegun them to death.  

I remember OMD2, needing to stagger and layer traps, with a variety, to deal with mobs with chain combos, all that seems to be forgotten here.  To futher make this an action game and not a tower defense game, many maps are simple and non-combinable.  Meaning each source of mob has its own lane, and you have to deal with them seperately.  Few are the maps that allow for proper channeling, funneling, cross killing and narrowing attack avenues.  There are even maps that have spawn points very near the rift, giving you very little time and room to deal with them. 

That seems to be where the challenge primarily lies in this game.  In having to run from one lane to another, often right next to the rift, and shoot or cut down the mobs yourself, rather than letting the traps handle it.  More fortnighty than a true TD - even an action TD in execution.  

The story is meh.  You get a cutscene here or there, some before map dialog, but thats really it.  The primary campaign is supposed to be about this ancient defender who was abandoned in orc territory and turned evil and is returning for vengence.  You see him on a cliff in the last mission and then he esplodes if you win.  Thats it.  Thats the whole thing.  Underwhelming.

To me this feels like a game that was rushed through production, for whatever reason.  Maybe Unchained was such a bomb, they needed profitable product out fast.  Maybe they had to rush to be a Stadia (lawl) launch title.  Doesn't matter.  Its a game that feels like corners were cut and design/mechanics principles were abandoned in favor of a quick turnaround.  Just my feeling on things from playing.

There are some positives.  The war scenarios and warmachines are NOT one of those positives.  They can only be used on specific maps and only in specific places, and are very expensive.  You are better served to use normal traps in normal areas, and massacre like a true war mage.  Scramble mode is great though.  Scramble mode is an Ironman endurance match where you have to play 5 maps back to back, each successive map adds a penalty and a bonus, and you have some choice about them.  Its a terrific mode for replayability and interesting experiences.  I got bonuses once for deadlier traps, cheaper traps with penalties for dying and it almost felt like a real OMD experience - putting out many traps, staying out of danger for the most part and letting my machines do the work.  

Bottom line, its a lesser version, a shadow, of OMD2.  There are a few new ideas, most fall flat.  It shifts the pendulum from trapping to avatar action (shooting/slicing/magic), so if you're wanting good tower defense gameplay, go elsewhere.  If you're a fan of the series, getting this on sale is a good move.  If you like simple 3rd person action against hordes of mobs, this is for you.

OMD3 is not a bad game, but it does not compare to OCD2 and that is a shame.

First off depending on your GPU ( running a RTX3080 ) there's a good chance it will max it out despite just running in 60fps despite the primitive cartoony graphics ( your electrical company will love you ) - so I hope you like to listen to your fans run at max for hours..

Second and more importantly the maps are not trap-based - you constantly have mutlple enemy spawn locations close to your rift with very few options to make the killboxes that the first 2 games were all about - WHY?

Thirdly you don't get enough money to build up your trapzones - when playing endless don't even expect more than 3seconds between waves so good luck selling and building before under attack again - and when enemy arches keep blowing up your blocks that is where your money will go in an endless cicle of frustration..

No workshop support either btw :(

So I'm finding myself stuck using archers in drowes because you simply do not have resources enough to make good trap-setups and all the time playing ( the campiagn is short and endless is limited ) I wish I was playing OMD2..

Honestly just play OMD2 it's a better game in all ways!

As a big fan of OMD 1 and OMD 2, this game feels like a very expensive DLC. It also takes the game further away from the tower-defense genre, and further into FPS. There is almost no new towers in OMD 3.

The voice acting is considerably worse than in the older games. I like the overall plot, but it failed to translate into cool traps. I finished the first campaign, and I'm unlikely to play it again.

Was it worth the buy? Meh, maybe. I got 10 hours of fun out of it, but compared to the older games; it's a bust.

[h1]💬Forewords:[/h1]
It frustrates me to have to write a negative review about a game in a franchise I like so much. But I do it to vent out some of my annoyance with the changes they've done to the game compared to Orcs Must Die! 1 and 2.

[h1]📉"Balance"[/h1]
This is the reason this game feels so unfulfilling. It seems like the game was tailor made to be less rewarding and less pleasant than it was before.

A lot of traps are unbalanced and many are so weak/expensive that they just don't cut it for Rift Lord, the highest difficulty (just to name a few: Decoy, Swinging Mace, Acid Geyser, Floor Scorcher). Nerfs when they happen usually make traps near useless while buffs are so meager they barely help change anything at all.

Weapons suffer from lack of balance too. Only a handful are worth using in higher difficulties and some are so weak they're not even worth considering (Elven Shortswords, Alchemist Satchel). Even weapon Mana Regen is completely absent.

The game does its darnest to counter the use of certain traps (Arcane Dragon and Saw Blade Launcher) for no reason other than the "balance". Such thing did happen before, but not the extent of OMD!3.

Characters have just marginal differences between Health and Mana, but no special trait beyond a small mobility skill triggered by double jumping, so all of them feels "samey" to play and nothing helps you try out new playstyles outside your own self-interest. Again, the reasoning behind this was, most likely, "balance". OMD!1 had Weavers and 2 had characters with a big enough difference in Mana and Health (and exclusive traps) to force you to adapt and learn or test new builds, but there is no such thing here.

In the end it seems Robot Ent. was too worried about balance, so much it ended up making for some very obnoxious level design and questionable enemy and gameplay choices. Whenever a company worries too much about game balance it inevitably ends up killing a lot of the fun in the game.

[h1]❌About War Scenarios:[/h1]
The War Scenarios in particular could've been done better. They drag on for too long and overstay their welcome. 

The War Machines can be only used in these maps. However, in most cases, you're better off arming places with regular traps instead of placing War Machines which is a pity. Later maps are designed in such a way that War Machines can feel downright detrimental and being a waste of money. 

Another thing is that you cannot place them inside buildings. This kills many would-be nice strategies and is just another factor in what makes War Machines so underwhelming for veteran players.

Even bosses add very little to the mix due to how easy they are to deal with. Scramble Mode shows they could've been into the regular game just fine (albeit not on EVERY wave), but they are present mostly in War Scenarios.

Having two currencies and enemies that should be specifically targeted by War Machines would do wonders to avoid the problem of War Machines being outdone by regular traps. Downsizing them or their effect a bit so they'd fit into buildings would also be a good option to place them in tandem with the regular traps.

[h1]⚖️How does it hold up against Orcs Must Die! 1 and 2?[/h1]
Sadly, comparing this game to the previous ones only serves to highlight the flaws of this game.

The game lacks pre-battle music except for War Scenarios.

Graphically, the HUD design was changed from colorful to a bland, minimalist, dull style:
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2793488611

Characters (and Orcs) have nowhere as many lines and start repeating the same phrases and one-liners very often which is particularly noticeable in longer games, like War Scenarios or Endless, and they don't even have wave start/end lines. And ALL of them share the same animations, including victory dance ones. Everything just feels lazy. Quality over quantity should be the lesson here.

The gameplay was simplified and some status effects and damage types were removed. Chill, an alternative to slow, is absent. Damage types; impact, cutting, piercing and explosive were reworked into a single type (Physical).

This simplification becomes a problem because Physical damage type is resisted by the vast majority of enemies in the game. And by vast majority I mean that it's easier to pick enemies that AREN'T resistant to it than the other way around. This renders Physical traps and weapons, one of the most common damage types, very ineffective.

On enemies, we have Fire Fiends. Fire Fiends are enemies that are as numerous as Orcs and are completely immune to fire element. Why? What made the developers assume bringing an entire enemy faction immune to an element was a good design decision? 

In previous games Fire and Frost Ogres (which are unexplainably absent here) were enough of a threat to force you to mix different elements, an entire faction of enemies feels just ridiculous.

Enemy design also became blander. Regular Orcs are all copy-pastes of each other instead of having a few distinct features (different skin colors or different armoring, like OMD!2 Orcs had) which could help players visually gauge how dangerous an Orc mob could be. 

Elementals also suffered from design change becoming boring, generic, looking enemies that could be seen in any fantasy game. Armored Ogres instead of wearing armor now seems like they just have bits of scraps all over them.

Many weapons are absent here too: Vampiric Gauntlets, Dwarven Missile Launcher, Polymorph Ring, Bone Amulet. As for traps that are missing: Boulder Chute, Healing Well, Acid Sprayer, Ice Vent, Dwarves, Mana Well, Coinforge, Void Wall, Spore Mushroom, Web Spinner.

Strategy-wise, the game became too focused on using a single core strategy: using Barricades to funnel enemies into a narrow space instead of being able to create big, open, killzones, which the game makes sure to discourage as much as possible with the small map design and weak/expensive crowd control and larger area hitting traps. Whereas Barricade killzones was a polite suggestion in previous games, in OMD!3 this strategy is so blatantly superior that not using it makes most of the maps more difficult.

Par times are needlessly demanding which punishes many, less aggressive, strategies as well. Previous games had maps with tough Par times, but OMD!3, again, exaggerates doing this in almost EVERY map.

The decision to cramp three storylines (the new Apprentices, the two ancient War Mages, and finding Max) with such limited time and levels to tell it was also a bad idea, as bad as leaving the face of the game, Maximilian, out of the 99% of the story. Again, everything feels rushed and ham-fisted at best and at worst half-heartedly which, for me, feels worse than not doing it in first place.

Kelsey and Egan, the newcomers, lack any of Max and Gabriella's charm with their lines being most about uninspired and soulless banter or clunky exposition.

Multiplayer also has a lot of missing features compared to the previous game: no in-game text chat, no pause, no in-game Voip, the inability to see your partner's loadout and not being able to see where they'll place a trap are the key ones. The host can also move to the next screen without your input before you upgrade which can be annoying.

Lastly, there are several bugs and glitches that were reported by players a year ago and most of them are still in the game. Like pre-order skins having no voice since *day 1*, no "Final Wave" warning in Rift Lord, clunky physics especially with Sappers and several Scramble Mode glitches in the wild.

[h1]💭Closing thoughts[/h1]
If you're coming from 1, 2 or Unchained you will notice the flaws right away, so this is a big cautious recommendation.

It's a game about traps, except the traps suck. Seriously. 

The traps feel like they do almost nothing, (Edit: My stats even show that 75% of my kills are from non-traps.) and that every problem has to be solved with guns, magic, and barricades. So solo play sucks because you can't rely on your traps to do anything, and you'll spend 50% of the time headshotting trolls and ogres. 

The best strategy in solo, is instead of laying tons of traps, is to use barricades to funnel them into a narrow area where you can gun them down.

The game is decent, but in my opinion, [b]Orcs Must Die 2 is better[/b]. I would recommend buying this game [u]only if it is on sale[/u]. This game could have been great, but it feels like the development was rushed.

For example, we have the [b]War Stages[/b], a very cool new feature. In these maps, you can use special [b]War Machine Traps[/b], but it is pointless to purchase these traps as [b]the normal ones are better and way cheaper[/b].

Also, this is the easiest game of the entire series so far: you just have to protect a [b]single Rift[/b] (easy killboxes), there are [b]no penalties when you die[/b] (the Orcs get the [i]Rift Rush[/i]* buff when you die), and there are [b]almost no flying enemies[/b] (so all your floor traps will work 95% of the time).

[u]It is not a bad game[/u]; if you like the genre, you should definitely give it a try. The new [b]Scramble[/b] mode is extremely fun.

Noticed a lot of reviews complain that traps are underpowered and that the game is built for 2 players, but I always play solo and didn't have much difficulty completing/5skulling the game on rift lord difficulty alone (it can be a bit tricky to learn which traps work well together etc though). Putting it simply, I loved OMD and OMD2, and this is technically the same. The graphics are definitely better, and certain aspects of the game (especially character control) are better. But... that's not really that surprising. Or at least, it should be expected, given the release dates respectively.

So why do I struggle to get into the game? I think it's primarily because of the traps... Or lack, thereof. It feels like it takes ages to get a good kill-box going, and by the time you do, your 6+ waves in, probably 1 from the end (or at the end...) and have killed ~50%, possibly more, of the orcs yourself.

You can argue balance issues, but I feel like this is intentional and will not be changed (considering the game is 1 year old, technically). And so each and every map I find myself in the exact same situation: Kill 80% of the orcs myself early waves, and slightly less towards the end. I thought the harder maps, or the onslaught (or whatever it is called) mode would be different - Alas, it's still kill 80% yourself early waves, but instead of 8/10 orcs, it's 80/100 orcs, and that's actually far worse!!

If I wanted to play a 1st/3rd person shooter killing obscure enemies, that's what I have L4D2 for... What I was hoping for was to be a master planner for in-house renovations to keep out the enemies for me whilst I munch on tea and biscuits. But I find myself tending to so much of the work myself regardless, that I don't even know why I bothered with them in the first place..

Overall, the kill box DOES become a thing, and you CAN watch them destroy hordes of enemies. But you CANNOT take your eyes of it for a second, because something will inevitably get through, and it takes time to get there - So that feeling of satisfaction takes a while to kick in.. Quite a while, comparatively to how long it lasts, as well.
Needs a workshop for mods and maps.

Orcs Must Die 3 is a nice and casual action tower defense game. Having played the second game, OMD 3 has a lot of the player power shifted towards the action part and much less on the defense building. The main weapons are powerful enough to hold early waves on their own and the freeze or petrify are crucial for stopping the big enemies including bosses. Traps serve best as crowd control in the form of flip traps, ceiling and wall stunners to keep the orcs busy enough until the players come to kill them, as traps are rarely good enough to hold a wave on their own and some enemies having elemental resistance rendering some traps useless. Some maps are impossible to beat without the barricades that redirect the enemy spawn points into a single corridor.

Like in the second game, it's a lot more fun to play in co-op and having the partner cover the other spawn point than having to do everything yourself. The weapon and trap mastery system would have been a cool idea, but skulls still need to be spent after meeting the requirements for them, luckily they aren't grindy. Melee weapons are a weird addition since there are ogres that chase the player to stun them, ranged is definitely the way to go. One weird mechanic is how the enemy speed up works in this game. The enemies only speed up when a player dies. This encourages one player to die on repeat while the other clears the early waves to reach par times required for the 5 skulls which I don't think is very fun for the player dying. Chasing high scores in endless is simply exhausting. The gameplay turns into perma freezing the big units to slowly chip away at their health because they get incredibly tanky. But the main levels are the main fun, especially with the war scenarios truly representing orcish hordes.

For achievement hunters:
The 2 paid DLCs are required. Most of the achievements are for completing all maps on rift lord with 5 skulls. Score chasing in Scramble is easily done with different trap effects.

Once upon a time maybe this was balanced differently; but by the late game and especially DLC you're playing a 3rd person shooter more than a tower defense. The maps become uninspired and theres little good synergy between traps and enemy variety by the end of the game. It starts out strong, there's maybe like 10 good maps in the whole thing. I've heard from others traps used to be a lot stronger and capable of dealing with threats and the player was more of an additional power- now the traps feel like they're just there to thin the weaker enemies so you can pour headshot after headshot into the larger ones.

I would not suggest this game to those who were a fan of the original. My biggest gripe is how worthless traps are. You will do so much of the killing yourself it just ruins the fun for me. I used to love just watching my awesome trap designs slaughter the orks. but its clear in this you need to take a major role in their destruction. which may be fun for others. but i prefer the tower defense style. its not a bad game. but just not what i was looking for. good luck :)

TL;DR If you have never played Orcs Must Die before, this is unfortunately not the place to start. 
Currently this game is basically a much less polished version of Orcs Must Die 2 with overall less content (roughly the same amount of loadout options but a lot less stages) for double the price (about the same after factoring in 2's DLCs)! So if you haven't already, definitely get OMD2 over this one! If you have and want more OMD, prepare for some very annoying and disappointing issues.

The new, extremely plastic looking design, the very basic UI, and the even more basic plot reveal Orcs Must Die 3 as a cheaply made and seemingly desperate attempt to revive the franchise after the Unchained disaster. I'm not gonna riff on the horrible humor and cringy dances, because they have always been part of this franchise, but for some reason this is the only time they felt really annoying to me. Probably because they seem so utterly soulless when the rest of the game just screams "shovelware". At least the orcs' battle chatter is as good as ever. 
If you're playing on a language other than English, be warned that the translation may not be complete! At least in German, some text and orc voice clips are still in English, which again does not speak well for the amount of love and care that went into this project...

The gameplay feels wonky at times and not nearly as impactfull compared to its predecessors. Many attacks really don't have much feedback anymore. The biggest offender for me personally being the Wind Belt, as grabbing an enemy with it never seems controlled but rather a dice throw against the physics engine, which may very well put your enemy under the floor, making it impossible for you to continue the stage.
Other fun bugs I encountered include:
-Progress for unlocking the unique upgrades for the Bladestaff not working at all [b] (this has just been fixed with a patch. After one year of this game being out on Stadia already, but better late than never I guess) [/b]
-All weekly challenges being playable, no matter if they're actually active ore not (not really a bad thing, but how on earth did they screw this up?) [b] (my bad, this is actually not a bug! see further down) [/b]
-Several problems for the non-host during coop, related to poor netcode and QA. For example: 
[list]
[*]Vorwicks teleport ability not stopping propperly, sending you flying forward instead of being the intended short blink.
[*]The Rapid Fire Ballista being completely unusable, because it stays firing in a fixed direction, no matter where you aim (this has apparently also been a long reported bug by the community, but was not fixed in the recent patch for whatever reason!)
[*]The coop partner not being able to select his own perks during the Scramble mode, instead being assigned a random one after every stage
[*]General laggyness that was never present with my same coop partner in OMD2
[/list]

The weekly challenges are apparently supposed to be all playable all the time. The "weekly" only reffers to the opportunity to place in the leaderboards for the challanges, which seems utterly pointless to me. At that point, why have a time gate at all? It's an absolute nitpick, but it  just seems like such a weird design decision.

In terms of traps and other loadout options, the overall amount ist roughly the same as in OMD2. There are some new additions, but also some very disappointing removals. The most heartbraking one for veterans possibly being the Coin Forge. In fact the money in OMD3 always feels way too tight to actually get an effective defense going. The moment you finally can afford the last crucial piece for your setup, it's already the final wave. A lot of the later stages - and many scramble challenges - basically rely on you constantly mopping up about half the wave yourself, because the traps are so ineffective. 
In order to get one of the two unique upgrades for a piece of equipment, you now have to grind some amount of kills or damage with it, instead of just unlocking them with skulls like in the previous games. So if you wanna test every trap and weapon to its fullest potential you are forced to do some grinding runs with inferior versions of them, which is not fun. Especially when they turn out to still be underwhelming after the upgrade.

With the recent patch Robot Entertainment has at least shown, that they have not completely abandoned the game, but honestly it seems like too little to late. Remember that this game was out on Google Stadia for [b] a year [/b] before it came to Steam. And they still have not fixed all the bugs that have been there since day one. Admittedly the amount of feedback the devs got during this time was probably not the most (har de har). 
Should they continue to develop on this game and add new content , it hopefully won't be in the form of paid DLC. Because right now and at this price, it feels like they're asking for a donation from the fanbase to maybe get the funding for an actually decent revival of the franchise going. Or they're just cheaply milking the last, sad drops from their horribly abused cow...

Compared to other error messages on the forum, mine was without any additional information.

It should not be forgotten that the "GameAnalytics" (BigData company for Realtime-Analytics, Event,- and Crossovertracking, Insights, Monitoring) service with connection to Amazon is active in the title, which is always activated, collects and send session data.

Customers are not informed about this behaviour on the sales page, nor do consumers have a chance to stop the behavior. If data is even recorded before the actual main menu is reached and permanently crashes, that is even more annoying.

Orcs Must Die 3 is a hybrid tower defence and third person action game where the player must use a combination of traps and their character’s melee or ranged weapons, to kill large waves of orcs and other monsters before they reach the rift located in your base.

[h1]The Good[/h1]

•	The basic gameplay loop of placing traps to deal with as many enemies as possible, and then finishing off the survivors yourself, will be familiar to fans of the previous games. Combat is enjoyably fast paced.

•	This game has a similar quality level as OMD 1 & 2, and is significantly better than Unchained, the terrible free to play game.

•	There’s a wide variety of enemies. In addition to the orcs there are ogres who have more health and can stun the player, trolls regenerate health, gnolls focus on attacking the player, kobolds are more difficult to hit because they’re smaller and run faster, fiends are immune to fire damage, and bats can fly over some traps. While the combat can occasionally feel chaotic with lots of enemies on screen, the colourful graphics make it easy to identify each different enemy type.

•	There are many different traps which can be placed on the floor, wall, or ceiling, and either deal physical or elemental damage (fire, ice, acid), or affect enemy movement in some way, for example by slowing them down or sending them flying through the air.

•	Good level design. Most maps have multiple entrances and different routes to your rift, but I didn’t feel disadvantaged by playing in single player, especially as my main tactic involves using barricades to force enemies into a single path, and then finding a narrow corridor to create a chokepoint of death. Some maps have acid pits or wall grinders that you can knock smaller enemies into for an instant kill.

•	It only takes around 10 hours to finish the campaign on medium difficulty, but you can spend more time trying to get a perfect 5 skull rating on each map, which requires not allowing even a single enemy to reach the rift.

•	There are also three extra game modes which add more value. Scramble asks you to beat 5 randomly selected maps from the campaign while giving you random buffs and debuffs affecting things like trap cost and damage, adding more enemies, giving them more health, increasing movement speed, or making them immune to certain damage types. You can play each map in Endless mode and just try to survive for as long as possible, and there are also weekly challenges.

•	I didn’t have any crashes or framerate issues, even with dozens of enemies and traps on screen.

•	Controls are rebindable and work great with mouse and keyboard.

[h1]The Bad[/h1]

•	Trap upgrade system discourages experimentation. Each trap can be upgraded 3 times to either increase damage, reduce cost, or reduce cooldown time, and then after you’ve used that trap to kill a few enemies you’ll be able to upgrade it with an extra effect, for example spike traps can do lightning damage and freeze traps can do acid damage. Its better to keep using the same 5-6 traps all the time and upgrade them to maximum, rather than buy new traps and do low damage. By the time I’d beaten the campaign, I hadn’t even unlocked half of the traps yet. Fully upgrading all traps will require replaying maps many times.

•	I wish it was possible to restart from the beginning of the current wave. Especially when trying to get a perfect 5 skulls, having to restart from the beginning just because 1 enemy got through on the final wave is annoying. 

[h1]The Recommendation[/h1]

There is some entertainment value to OMD3, either in 2p co-op or solo, but it also suffers from a lack of polish in a variety of areas which makes it worse than its predecessors.

[h1]Map Design[/h1]
[list]

[*]In previous OMD, maps are designed like a puzzle for single players to complete, with the option of 2p multiplayer in OMD2. In OMD3 however, maps are designed with more multiplayer focus in mind, which in my opinion makes it less appropriate as a single player experience (though not impossble), especially with the trap nerfed and bullet-sponge enemy health increased, which makes them unreliable to actually stop one lane while while you focus on another.

[*] Some kind of major F’ up occurred in production that has allowed map 16 (the basement) to be included in the final product, a large portion of the map (including the basement floor) serve no purpose, completely disconnected from any of the three routes. 

[/list]

[h1]Gameplay changes[/h1]
[list]

[*]Traps nerfed and number of orcs increased (which in part makes traps less effective). I don’t mind for the more active gameplay requiring you to actively shoot orcs, but it does get dull with the limited variety of enemies, particularly in endless mode.

[*]Big enemies like ogres and trolls (particularly armored trolls) seem to be more bullet-spongy than previous entries, requiring dozens (or hundreds) of headshots to put down. Because the big enemies requires so much time to kill, freezes/petrifies become practically mandatory to stop bullet sponges from reaching the rift. This design choice contributes to the lack of variety, since all light and medium enemies tend to die to traps before they get close to the rift, you’re only ever shooting at the same few enemies by the end-game.

 [*] Physics traps are significantly less reliable in OMD3, partly because different weight classes are affected much more drastically differently, and partly because the maps aren’t well designed to fling orcs into the air.

[*]Wall grinder no longer sucks orcs into them and reduces them into giblets, it just passively damages orcs as they pass by, which is pretty lame.

[*] Archers are nerfed, which I’m fine with, they were rather ridiculously OP in previous games.

[*]I’ve used the crossbow in OMD1, which requires careful aiming and patience for accuracy to reset between shots. I’ve use the domination staff in OMD 2 which is a bit OP in crowd control. Weapons in OMD3 in contrast is much more spammy and requires less careful consideration. You’re practically required to spam headshots with a ranged weapon (gatling gun or crossbow, which uses no mana to spam, any inaccuracy spread just means you have to stand closer while shooting non-stop). Every weapon that doesn’t do headshots, such as the melee weapons, are practically useless unless they have good secondary properties (eg. freezes).

[*]Traps block bullets, which is really annoying, and disincentivizes use of traps that pops out and blocks at head level.

[*]camera angle often has your character's head blocking view of orcs, particularly when up close.

[*] One of the DLCs introduces cyclopses, which take (extra-)extra damage to the head; I'm not sure the devs realize it doesn't help with enemy variety if you're doing the same exact thing (headshots) with them as with every other enemy type under the sun.

[/list]

[h1]UI[/h1]
[list]

[*]Campaign main page lacks details about enemy details, you have to go inside to check the enemy list, then go back out if you want to respec skill points. Campaign main page is also lacking in map details, you can’t view how many floors are present in the level and switch between floors. (This was also the case in previous games, didn't have to adopt it tho)

[*]Trap UI lacks details about damage, cooldown, etc.

[*] Lacks bestiary/compendium to read about all enemy types outside of campaign.

[*] Character select screen lacks details about their jump abilities.

[*] The unique upgrades to equipment and traps has a questionable design: in OMD2, you can freely switch between 2 unique upgrades upon purchasing either; to switch between unique upgrades in OMD3, you have to refund skulls for that equipment and pick the unique upgrade you want to switch to, and re-upgrade its stats. I don't understand why you want to give players extra busy work for something that is done in one click in the previous game.

[*] Previous games’ stylized UIs looks better than the purple screens in this one.

[*] The big splashy headshot indicator from the previous OMD1 is downgraded to a tiny one, which does make it less satisfying to hit headshots, along with how many of them are required to kill bigger enemies.

[/list]
[h1]Multiplayer[/h1]
[*] Multiplayer lobby needs work, no passwords means randos can join while you're waiting for friend.

[*]no communication available in lobby

[*]no voice-comms or text chat in-game, only a limited chat wheel (developed for console peasants, probably) by which it is impossible to communicate plans and strategies in any sort of depth.

[*] There doesn’t seem to be a way to view MP scoreboard without opening a MP lobby, where people can randomly join regardless of whether you intend to play.

The game design is very loosey-goosey. I really, really enjoyed OMD1 back in the day but this does not feel like a culmination or development.

For one, there's a lot of options but most of them are clearly sub-optimal. Even in the weirdest stages, the way to get the best score is to build the same exact killbox and route everything through it. There was exactly one mission where I couldn't get all entrances routed to a killbox with walls/ceiling, so I had to use only floor traps. Besides that none of the obvious bait laid by level designers (lava pits for pushing in, and such) were as efficient as the standard killbox. Decisions don't mean anything if one option is clearly superior. (There's something to be said for player expression as well, but it doesn't apply here unless you're self-imposing a challenge because you're bored of dunking on monsters the same way over and over.)

Another example of loose design: in the final mission, enemies can spawn from anywhere at any time. This might appear to violate the idea the game has built the entire time, that you get advance warning of where the enemies will come from and get to plan out your emplacements in advance (i.e. basically the whole point of the game). But don't worry, you can kill them all with your standard weapon. Ahh, okay, so you need to watch the map and go attend to emergencies, okay, I'll give it a pass. Until you play for 30 minutes and suddenly toward the end of the entire stage, no, you CAN'T kill them all with just your weapon, you NEED traps for them because suddenly it spawns a crazy number. OK so this completely violates the basic design language and invalidates the entire design. And what's worse, when you say "got it, I will move the killbox ultra-close to the end zone so it can catch everything" and restart the level, the "anywhere at anytime" spawns turn out to be HARD-CODED. Meaning there is even less reason to hide that information from the player. It's just a big middle finger to the player's first attempt at the level, and the entire reason why, in the FIRST GAME, they realized they needed to show where enemies would come from before the level starts. And at the end of it all once you know it's going to pull that BS, it's not even different, just the same killbox as always.

These are a few particularly bad examples but the whole game feels like this. They didn't know where to go but they had a profitable franchise and so they churned out another one, with no clear idea of how to go bigger and better. (The "big big battlefield with big big traps" thing is bogus, because it's usually better not to waste money on the battlefield and just let them into the end area with... you guessed it, same killbox as always.)

The art is quite polished, but the pathfinding and player controls are very buggy. Sometimes enemies will walk through a barricade, or you won't be able to fire your weapon until you stop moving because it thinks you're still sprinting when you're not, or any number of other annoyances.

I played it to the end (kind of a short campaign, disappointing) and it killed some hours decently enough, but overall I'm just... disappointed in the execution.

I've been a fan of the Orcs Must Die! series for quite some time, and I've particularly enjoyed diving into the endless mode. However, it's disappointing to say that the current state of the game has introduced some significant problems that are seriously affecting my experience.

One of the most glaring issues revolves around the Unreal Engine 4 (UE4) that the game utilizes. While playing the endless mode, I've encountered repeated fatal errors stemming from the UE4. To my dismay, this issue has cropped up three times out of my seven total runs on endless. It's disheartening to witness top scores on leaderboards being achieved through exploiting these glitches, which casts a shadow over the game's competitive integrity.

The problematic state of the game, coupled with its persisting bugs and glitches, compels me to share my negative feedback. Despite the passage of time and the lessons learned from the shortcomings of Orcs Must Die! Unchained, it's disheartening that an unfinished and buggy game has been released.

Unfortunately, even two months after my initial encounter with the fatal crashes, no fixes have been implemented, and technical support remains unresponsive. This lack of attention from the development team paints a concerning picture.

Fast forward to three months later, and the situation remains unchanged. The developers continue to overlook these issues, leaving players frustrated and unable to fully enjoy the game. The game feels as if it's stuck in a pre-alpha stage, with the prospect of more resets looming.

Bugs have undoubtedly marred what could have been an enjoyable experience. It's disappointing to observe the developers' apparent lack of concern for these issues. This sentiment is further compounded by the release of new DLC that introduces even more bugs while failing to address the existing crashes.

A year has passed since my initial encounters with these problems, and it's disheartening to note that not a single response has been received from the development team. Technical support seems nonexistent for the game, leaving players like me to deal with a multitude of bugs, crashes, and cheaters. Even the scoring system is riddled with inconsistencies.

As we approach the two-year mark, a new patch has been introduced. However, it's disheartening to see that the major issues that have plagued the game remain unaddressed. The Orcs' AI still leaves much to be desired, and barricades continue to break unexpectedly. Archers, cannons, and ballistas still exhibit subpar AI, rendering them ineffective against hordes of enemies. Crashes persist, the lack of in-game communication is glaring, and even the basic game resolution settings are broken.

Additionally, Robot Entertainment has reset the leaderboards due to trap balance adjustments. Consequently, players are now unable to register new scores, as they must achieve new high scores on all maps in order to record their latest achievements.

It's baffling that ROBOT Entertainment seems incapable of rectifying the technical issues that plague the game, preventing players from enjoying it to the fullest. The journey with Orcs Must Die! 3 has been marred by the frustrating persistence of these problems, and it's a shame that the potential for a great experience remains largely untapped due to the lack of adequate fixes.

Orcs run from the entrance to the exit, and you wound, maim, crush, smash, slash, stab, shoot, burn, fry, shock, melt, freeze, explode, confuse, charm, explode some more, slow-while-doing-some-combination-of-all-of-the-others, and probably a few other things... them until they're all dead or they overwhelm you.

I adore this series, and OMD3 has not disappointed me at all. Chances are that the game isn't going to result in 1,000 hours of gameplay, and that's fine. It's not an MMO, and it's not a AAA game.

However, It -is- a massive amount of good, innocent fun for the whole family*.

*Depending on your family and definition of innocent, also with the understanding that co-op is two players only. So if there are more than two of you, pick the family member you like most.

If you are new to the franchise then I HIGHLY RECOMMEND skipping this entry entirely and starting with the better, Orcs Must Die 2!.

OMD2! Is better in NEARLY every way. Level design, character design, content, skins, weapons, traps, bugs, story, UI, soul, etc.

OMD3! does have some new traps/weapons/trinkets, but also completely removes or changes ones from the previous entry. 
OMD3! does only TWO things better than OMD2!:
One, you can refund individual traps (but not the trap itself!). 
Two, dying no longer counts against your rift points, at least on Warmage (default) difficulty. 
Whether this is better or not is debatable, but I like it personally. 

Things I don't like in OMD3! (Minor playable character spoilers ahead):

-Forced to play two new characters who, while not terrible, are no replacement for the second game's Max and Gabriela.

-Characters no longer have different health/mana pools as far as I can tell, and only have different "secondary jumps", which mostly suck compared to those of Max and Gabriela. This makes Cygnus feel unplayable, comparatively. 

-Some things are still bugged, like the Bladestaff, which cannot be leveled up unless you have a pre-order version of the weapon. Mind you this game came out like a year ago as a Stadia exclusive so.... wtf.

-Skins suck. Max is the ONLY character with a skin that isn't a simple recolor, and its just a worse version of his Classic skin. All skins in this game are kinda lame, and there is only ONE per character, with the exception of Max, who gets one PLUS the same recolor theme as everyone else.

-The UI is super simplistic and soulless compared to the second game. Every character has the same victory dance too, which I am pretty sure Max and Gabs had separate dances in OMD2! There is still different dances for how many skulls you got though, at least two (4 Skull and 5 are the only I've seen).

-Flyers have been COMPLETELY removed until the (short) secondary campaign which i think was originally DLC before OMD3! came to Steam. Again, why remove things from a sequel that worked in the original without a suitable replacement or REASON to be removed outside of laziness?

-This might be a problem in the second game too, I really don't remember, but SOME maps are made in such a way that playing alone makes it VERY difficult to 5 Skull (Perfect) a stage, even on Warmage difficulty. 

Finally. Siege battles (The "big new thing") are boring, at least on Warmage difficulty. They take way too long, are not really challenging or even much of a spectacle. They can all be handled pretty much with some barricades and a couple of condensed super kill boxes, which are easy to make with how much coin you are given for these maps. One can ignore MOST of the new SIEGE ONLY traps, after the first siege mission, because why bother with them!? Also, everyone of them has a BS mechanic. Usually it is a Boss being introduced in the Final Wave that has some BS mechanic that will ruin whatever you have set up. IF you have played the map before, its no problem because you know its coming. But if you were doing really well on your first run and one of these things shows up and ruins your perfect score with absolutely no warning before the Final Round, then you might get upset. 

(EDIT): A recent patch has fixed a few of the major bugs, and made some traps a little better (usable). The review still stands however, as the primary issues with it would require more than just a couple patches. If they fix and add enough, to make it on par with 2, I will consider a positive review. A sequel should never detract the good things of its predecessor, without suitable replacement.

OMD3 does have 1 fatal flaw. If an orc DOES NOT move out of the rift he cannot be killed. If he cannot be killed you cannot kill all orcs. If you cannot kill all orcs you CANNOT WIN.

I like Orcs Must Die games. Although this one lacks the content that previous games had, I liked Orcs Must Die 3 too. To sum it up, you build traps, kill orcs and defend your base. It has a simple premise, and I like it. The graphics look beautiful. The soundtrack is nice. Just like the previous games, the humorous storytelling is good. At the end of the day it's a good game but in future I prefer playing the first game or the second. Here are my reasons for that:
- There are lots of new traps in this game, but most of them are useless. There are only 6-7 traps that are worth using, rest of them are just waste of time. I prefer quality over quantity.
- War Scenarios! These levels are huge, and they throw hundreds of orcs at you. They spawn from 3-4 different spawn points and trying to control them is exhausting. While playing these levels most of the time, I was praying for the level to end. I wasn't having fun, it felt like a chore.
- Co-op element. It is very clear that most of the levels are designed for co-op. They didn't think of the single player aspect while designing these levels. You hardly get breathing room between the waves and trying to get a 5 star while playing single player is too hard in some levels. In previous games I always had the time to mess around and have fun.
- The main campaign is too short. If you are not a perfectionist and not trying to get a 5 star on every level you can easily finish it in two days.
Overall I had fun while playing it but I think first and second games are superior.
